entities.name: Andy declares ambition to become the biggest star in the world
entities.description: Andy tells George that he wants to be the biggest star in the world, expressing grand ambition despite claiming to have no talent.

entities.name: George expresses surprise at Andy's hubris
entities.description: George reacts with visible surprise to Andy's bold declaration of wanting to be the biggest star in the world.

entities.name: Andy rejects being labeled a comedian
entities.description: Andy clarifies to George that he is not a comedian and claims to have no talent, describing himself instead as a song-and-dance man.

entities.name: George notices a booger in Andy's nostril
entities.description: George looks at Andy and sees a large booger hanging from his nostril, causing him to cringe in discomfort and hesitation.

entities.name: Waitress serves unappetizing health food to Andy and George
entities.description: A waitress delivers two plates of unappealing 1970s health food, including seaweed, beans, and stringy paste, to Andy and George's table.

entities.name: George frowns at the appearance of the food
entities.description: George reacts negatively to the sight of the health food served to them, expressing disapproval through a frown.

entities.name: Andy enthusiastically recommends the lotus root
entities.description: Andy expresses delight in the meal and specifically recommends the lotus root to George with genuine enthusiasm.

entities.name: Andy cleans his hands with a Handi-wipe
entities.description: Andy uses a Handi-wipe to clean his hands before eating, demonstrating a particular hygiene ritual.

entities.name: Andy compulsively arranges food into geometric patterns
entities.description: Andy meticulously organizes the components of his meal into structured formations, such as beans in pinwheels and sprouts in piles.

entities.name: George observes Andy's unusual food arrangement behavior
entities.description: George watches Andy's compulsive food arranging with curiosity and growing concern, trying to understand Andy's peculiar habits.

entities.name: Lunch Meeting At Bohemian Health Food Restaurant
entities.description: Andy and George meet over lunch at a 1970s-style health food restaurant to get to know each other, engaging in conversation amid awkward and revealing moments.
entities.summary: Andy and George meet over lunch at a 1970s-style health food restaurant to get to know each other, engaging in conversation amid awkward and revealing moments.

entities.name: Bohemian health food restaurant
entities.description: A specific restaurant setting with a distinct bohemian atmosphere where Andy and George are having lunch.

entities.name: Andy
entities.description: A man who aspires to be the biggest star in the world and exhibits particular habits around food and self-presentation during a lunch meeting with George.
entities.summary: A performer engages in imaginative character voices and singalongs for Carol, while another man abruptly stops sobbing and faces confrontation in a dangerous neighborhood, highlighting contrasting emotional performances and abrupt behavioral shifts in different settings.

entities.name: George
entities.description: A man meeting with Andy at a health food restaurant, reacting with surprise and discomfort to Andy's statements and behavior.
entities.summary: A man observes Andy's comedy act with interest, compliments his performance, meets him at a restaurant, and later acts as his representative, presenting demands to network executives after Andy refuses a sitcom role.

entities.name: hippie waitress
entities.description: A waitress at the Bohemian health food restaurant who serves unappetizing health food to Andy and George.

entities.name: Handi-wipe
entities.description: A small wipe used by Andy to clean his hands before arranging his food in geometric patterns.

entities.name: Lotus root
entities.description: A food item in Andy's meal that he enthusiastically recommends to George.

entities.name: giant moist booger
entities.description: A noticeable nasal discharge hanging from Andy's nostril, observed with discomfort by George.

entities.name: hippie culture
entities.description: A cultural aesthetic reflected in the restaurant's staff, decor, and food choices, associated with 1970s countercultural values.

entities.name: George expresses uncertainty about booking Andy due to unclear performance category
entities.description: George tells Andy that while he shows promise, he doesn't fit into established performance formats like stand-up or film, making it difficult to know where to book him.

entities.name: Andy declares ambition to perform at Carnegie Hall
entities.description: Andy brightly states his desire to play Carnegie Hall, presenting it as a serious goal rather than a joke.

entities.name: Andy performs ritualistic cleaning of silverware before eating
entities.description: Andy dips his silverware twice in the water glass and dries it with his napkin in a precise, ritualistic manner.

entities.name: George notices Andy's booger has moved to the other nostril
entities.description: George observes with confusion that the booger in Andy's nose has seemingly switched nostrils.

entities.name: Andy bows head in silent prayer before eating
entities.description: Before eating, Andy bows his head in a moment of silent prayer, prompting George to raise an eyebrow in surprise.

entities.name: Andy proclaims desire for intense audience emotional reactions
entities.description: Andy declares that he doesn't want easy laughs but instead wants audiences to experience strong, conflicting emotions, even walking out angry, as part of a great performance.

entities.name: Andy triumphantly eats a bean after dramatic declaration
entities.description: After proclaiming his artistic vision, Andy eats a single bean with a triumphant expression.

entities.name: George points out booger to Andy using a napkin
entities.description: Unable to ignore it any longer, George hands Andy a napkin and points to his nose to indicate the booger.

entities.name: Andy removes fake booger and stores it in a box
entities.description: Andy takes out a rubber booger from his nose and carefully places it in a small box, treating it as a collectible.

entities.name: Andy plans to sell used props as celebrity memorabilia
entities.description: Andy explains that after becoming famous, he intends to sell his used props, like the fake booger, as authentic items 'Worn by Andy Kaufman'.

entities.name: George becomes convinced of Andy's brilliance and agrees to represent him
entities.description: After Andy's performance and explanation, George shifts from skepticism to admiration, calling Andy insane but possibly brilliant, and agrees to work with him.

entities.name: George and Andy shake hands to seal professional agreement
entities.description: George extends his hand in agreement, Andy accepts, and they shake hands in a moment of mutual commitment and significance.

entities.name: Andy apologizes for his past wrestling behavior on live television
entities.description: Andy, appearing pale and dazed, expresses regret for his past actions as a villainous wrestler, explaining it was just a role and not his true self, while addressing Jerry Lawler and David Letterman on the show.

entities.name: Jerry Lawler and David Letterman react dismissively to Andy's apology
entities.description: Lawler and Letterman show they are unimpressed by Andy's emotional apology, with Letterman pointing out Andy's past inflammatory remarks and Lawler accusing him of treating serious matters as jokes.

entities.name: Andy defends himself against Lawler's accusations on live television
entities.description: Andy stammers and attempts to justify himself, stating there was no reason for Lawler to intentionally harm him, showing visible distress during the confrontation.

entities.name: Jerry Lawler insults Andy as a wimp during the talk show
entities.description: Lawler escalates the tension by calling Andy a wimp, further provoking him in front of the audience and host.

entities.name: Andy accuses Lawler of being poor white trash in a heated outburst
entities.description: Overwhelmed and upset, Andy lashes out at Lawler, shouting that he is 'poor white trash,' marking a turning point in the confrontation.

entities.name: Jerry Lawler slaps Andy, causing him to fall from his chair
entities.description: Enraged by Andy's insult, Lawler suddenly stands and violently slaps him, sending Andy crashing to the floor, leaving the audience and crew in stunned silence.

entities.name: Paul Shaffer plays rockabilly music to break the tension
entities.description: In an attempt to recover from the shocking violence, Paul Shaffer quickly begins playing a rockabilly tune on the piano to cover the awkward silence.

entities.name: Andy erupts in rage and screams threats at Jerry Lawler
entities.description: After getting up from the floor, Andy becomes unhinged, shouting profanities at Lawler, threatening to sue him and vowing revenge while pounding the desk.

entities.name: Andy storms out of the talk show in a fit of anger
entities.description: Overcome with emotion and fury, Andy leaps up, screams at Lawler one final time, and storms off the set, leaving the studio in shock.

document_metadata.title: 171、INT. FUNERAL HOME - DAY
document_metadata.summary: Andy's funeral film ends with a song, the casket vanishes behind a curtain, and mourners are left uncertain, some believing he might reappear, as silence falls.

entities.summary: A performer engages in imaginative character voices and singalongs for Carol, while another man abruptly stops sobbing and faces confrontation in a dangerous neighborhood, highlighting contrasting emotional performances and abrupt behavioral shifts in different settings.
